checkpoints.top_reasoning: No murder facts yet. Vincent's expensive objections, Tess's family tension, restitution disputes for Robin/Penny, and Brie's donor friction suggest possible motives only. No meaningful culprit ranking is justified.
checkpoints.naturalness: Occupations and concise voices are distinct enough, though nearly every introduction uses a polished joke or pointed warning. Many overlapping art/provenance professions may blur during a thirty-player game.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Artie's proposed firing is the clearest personal motive. Brie and Minnie plausibly touch private service and privacy arrangements; poison bottle and crest glass stand out as possible method objects. Anya's provenance shortcut, Claire's disputed bowl, and Frank/Elle's unsafe alcove add other conflicts. Who requested the misleading equipment-fault entry is unclear. None of the documents proves murderous behavior.
checkpoints.naturalness: Documents build an interconnected event with donor control as a coherent conflict. Frequent draft/proposed/not-approved qualifications feel conspicuous and slow the drama. Cheese ticket and gift glass feel like puzzle props, but credible ones.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Death following private toast strengthens attention to glass, catering/service access and historical poison. The notice supplies no cause or time precision, so I retain the preceding ranking. Artie's threatened resignation is still a motive even though unaccepted, but no direct act implicates him.
checkpoints.naturalness: A board office announcing donor death and immediately clarifying pending paperwork is plausible institutional self-protection, yet the repeated proposal disclaimers feel authorially emphatic. This is a very thin evidence checkpoint.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Hugh's forced admission could destroy his firm; Cary is being blackmailed over damage and coerced into object checks, giving a stronger access-related motive. Artie faces removal, Brie has private-toast preparation, Barb deliberately allowed missing monitoring, Faye faces blackmail, and Tess hints succession stakes. All have reasons for anger, few have shown lethal intent. Sue's involvement in the troublesome acquisition also matters.
checkpoints.naturalness: Voices have occupational detail and some memorable humor. However almost every statement repeats Grant demanded control/credit, I made a compromised earlier choice, I objected or withdrew paperwork. The donor has conveniently offended nearly everyone in one evening. Strong individual secrets but extremely uniform arc structure.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Cary's condition-check coercion now intersects an active bottle emptied in staff preparation storage, making him a leading suspect. Brie can reach the individual glass throughout service; Minnie, Barb and Chip also have relevant event/security/object access. Vincent painted the bottle and may know its appearance, though access is unestablished. Shared food/punch negative narrows method to individual glass, but contamination could happen during unattended setup or later service. Concealed split suggests deliberate opening and possible resealing.
checkpoints.naturalness: The unattended bespoke glass is a workable murder opportunity. The bottle's lender inert-liquid declaration versus active cyanide is a good discrepancy. Evidence arrives in very compact, remarkably conclusive laboratory rows; absence of investigation detail is acceptable for a party puzzle but feels schematic.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Brie directly visited the set glass carrying culinary flavoring and left its container, a ready explanation for poison delivery. Tess ordered the personalized glass and visited its unattended place; Dada, Barb and Minnie also specifically accessed that place. Anya had a spare cupboard key and saw stored bottle. Chip applied its closure; Art E Fact and Hugh knew original-contents discrepancy. Cary's wrapped transfer and later freight-lift problem reduce his apparent glass opportunity, although not independently proven. Too many object handlers and private-room visitors remain for an obvious culprit.
checkpoints.naturalness: Second statements advance real logistics and secrets, but almost every character altered, withheld, clipped, moved or replaced some document/image. This creates a repetitive correction-and-confession rhythm. The density of suspicious benign errands to exactly the bottle or toast place feels arranged. Brie announcing an ingredient visit is striking but can fairly be innocent drink preparation.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Chip rises: his new closure band matches generic scrap in poisoned glass and he falsified the treatment date, knew bottle danger, and had access; the scrap is explicitly not a unique match so this is not proof. Brie's clean ingredient container weakens simple adulterated-flavoring theory but does not exclude direct poison addition. Tess, Dada, Barb and Minnie retain room opportunity; Anya retains bottle access. Robin and Paige now definitely entered private interview with set glass, contradicting my earlier assumption they were peripheral. Many financial disputes were settled, weakening Hugh/Cary/others. No timed pairing of bottle access and glass access yet singles out one person.
checkpoints.naturalness: The evidence is unusually crowded with corrections, credits, withdrawn demands and settlement attachments. Almost everyone repairs their earlier ethical failure, producing tidy parallel redemption rather than varied reactions to murder. Strong fair clarification of physical versus image props, but excessive explicit exclusions read like an answer-key cleanup. Dates October 29/30 are internally comprehensible though the event date has not been anchored here.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Hugh is now overwhelmingly strongest. He asserts a canceled original-contents condition and an inert substituted delivery; seller fulfillment explicitly says original contents retained and no cancellation/substitution instruction received, intake already held complete seller condition, and laboratory found active cyanide. This is a specific falsifiable account of murder means, beyond admitting unrelated bowl fraud. Other suspects chiefly confirm known documents. Hugh's preview presence is not stated as directly as others', and exact glass/cupboard movement is not supplied, so a reconstructed timeline remains incomplete. Chip retains closure access, false insurance date, and matching generic material; Brie had direct dosing opportunity; Barb arranged camera blackout. These remain practical alternatives if Hugh's falsehood conceals negligence rather than murder, but the unique final contradiction dominates the supplied puzzle.
checkpoints.naturalness: Final round has one dramatic falsification surrounded by near-universal documentary self-correction. Hugh's changed account is conspicuous even without detailed time reconstruction. Character voices still differ, but repeated read-the-column/look-at-the-picture clarifications and ethical admissions make many speakers function as exhibit interpreters. The night has too many neatly resolved financial/publicity scandals. Murder method is plausible, while possession of historical active poison on an open museum bench despite warnings strains institutional practice.

final_feedback: Strongest suspect: Hugh Bidder, 9/10, because his final neutralization/substitution story directly contradicts seller fulfillment and laboratory findings. Remaining alternatives: Chip Patina (seal material, false date, bottle handling), Brie DeVivre (individual drink flavoring and direct glass access), Barb Dwyer (intentional recording blackout), with Anya/Tess/Dada/Minnie having some access but less incriminating late evidence. No premature obvious identification in stages 1-7; stage 8 supplies the first dominant unique contradiction. At stage 7 Chip led without a decisive case. Thirty voices have useful occupational details but closely repeated arcs: donor overreach, concealed compromise, document withdrawal, then correction/settlement and embarrassed accountability. Numerous print/image misreadings become mechanically repeated. The bottle-to-glass chain lacks a unique material match or direct movement witness, leaving Hugh's motive/access case less fully proved than his decisive lie.
